Product Name: Exceptional by ASDA Italian Black Olive Breadsticks 120g
Comments:
Overall impression: Premium look and branding, badly undercut by packaging that fails on opening and product that arrives mostly broken. Taste is acceptable but not exceptional, so it doesn't currently live up to the "Exceptional" name.

Shelf appeal: Strong. The dark green and gold box looks upmarket and every bit a premium product on the shelf.

Packaging: The biggest let-down. The carton didn't open cleanly. It tore jaggedly across the top and down the side rather than opening at a proper seam, which instantly killed the premium feel before I'd even seen the product.

Product condition: Once poured out, only one breadstick in the whole pack was still intact and the rest had snapped into short segments. For an artisan, premium-positioned product that's poor. I didn't directly compare to the premium offer, but from memory that level of breakage hasn't been the case. On condition and packaging alone, it doesn't benchmark well even against a standard breadstick, let alone a premium one.

Taste and texture: Reasonable. Good visible black olive and a nice rustic look, but slightly soft for a breadstick when I'd expect a crisp snap. The family enjoyed them and the whole pack was eaten, so no complaint on flavour, just not a standout for a premium line.

Bottom line: Looks the part on shelf, but the packaging tearing on opening and the broken sticks pull it well below premium expectations, and the soft texture stops the taste from rescuing it. Priorities: a pack that opens cleanly and protects the sticks in transit, and a firmer crunch. Get those right and the branding and flavour are already there to support a premium benchmark.

The concept of pre-sliced frozen red onion may appeal to customers looking for convenience and time savings. However, the large pack size limits its versatility, particularly for smaller households or recipes that require only a small amount of onion.
The onion is pre-cut into strips and frozen, which means the customer cannot easily adapt it for different cooking methods or recipes. In addition, adding the frozen onion directly to a hot pan causes significant oil splatter, making it less convenient and potentially messy to cook with.
The packaging is clear and practical, making it easy to understand the product and its intended use.
Compared with buying fresh red onions, this product offers convenience but sacrifices flexibility and freshness. Personally, I prefer fresh vegetables that can be prepared according to the specific recipe, so this product would not be my preferred choice despite the time-saving aspect.

Comments:
This feedback is kind of outside the initial brief, but my background is in ecommerce development, and I've worked in this area for nearly 30 years which means I'm a bit sensitive to things that get in the way of customers being able to buy products easily ??

The first thing I noticed is the list of brands search filter is ordered by the number of products per brand, as a customer I don't know how many products match a brand, so I have no way to quickly get to the brand I want. If I have opened that filter my intent is to look for a specific brand and in most places that list would be alphabetical so seeing a list that isn't causes me to pause & think, a blocker to adding a product to the cart.

All Asda brands should be at the top of that list, when they are at the moment it's because they have the most products in that category, the other brands like Exceptional, Free From  and Essentials were usually lower on the list.




To test the hypothesis that the order of the list is stopping some customers from adding items to their baskets I would conduct an A/B test. Show one configuration to a set of customers and the other to another set then look at the number of Asda brand products each cohort adds to their basket.

I don't know if our relationship with the 3rd parties who make the changes to the site enables that kind of testing and analysis.

Secondly, I kept seeing non-Asda brands when filtering by an Asda brand. I can't recreate it now so maybe it was a problem with the Algolia data.

Comments:
Unfortunately, this meal wasn't enjoyable and I wouldn't recommend it.

The mashed potato was probably the best part of the meal. It wasn't terrible, but it had a very basic, school-dinner style texture and flavour. On its own I'd rate the mash around 3-4/5.

The bacon was the biggest disappointment. It looked overcooked, tasted very fatty, and had an unpleasant flavour that I found quite off-putting. It really detracted from the overall meal.

The liver pieces were a good size and the texture was what I'd expect from liver, so no complaints there. However, the flavour had a floral note that simply didn't appeal to my palate and didn't work well with the rest of the dish.

The onion gravy was acceptable, but overall the combination of flavours just didn't come together for me. Between the poor-quality bacon and the floral taste of the liver, this is not a meal I would choose again.

Pros: Good-sized liver pieces, acceptable mash and gravy.
 Cons: Overcooked, fatty-tasting bacon; liver flavour was overly floral; overall dish lacked balance.

Would I buy again? No.

Comments:
???? The Minions of Vegetables
Let's be honest, it's corn on the cob. It's not winning any Michelin stars, but it does exactly what you want it to do.
These were sweet, juicy, cooked well, and made a great side dish. The sort of thing you add to your plate without much thought, then end up finishing before everything else.
Why the Minions?
Because they're simple, cheerful, and somehow make everything around them better. They're never the main attraction, but you'd definitely notice if they didn't turn up.
Sweet and juicy
Quick and easy to prepare
Goes with almost any meal
Easy to find in-store and online
Overall: A reliable side dish that does its job with a smile. Nothing fancy, nothing complicated, just tasty corn making dinner a little bit better.

???? The Hobbits of Snacks
These chopped apricots are proof that you don't need fancy packaging or exotic ingredients to be good. They're sweet, tasty, and perfect for chucking into a packed lunch.
Before you know it, half the bag has disappeared and you're wondering who ate them. (Spoiler: it was probably you.)
Why Hobbits?
Because they're small, humble, and easy to underestimate. Then somehow they've vanished and you're immediately looking for second breakfast.
Naturally sweet and tasty
Great for lunchboxes and snacking
Easy to find in-store and online
Bag seems to empty itself somehow
Overall: Nothing flashy, nothing dramatic, just really good apricots doing really good apricot things. The sort of snack that quietly wins you over one handful at a time.

????? The Clark Kent of Pizzas
This pizza won't be appearing on any "Best Meal Ever" lists, but it does a solid job when you need a quick and easy dinner.
The cheese was tasty, it cooked well, and there was nothing to complain about. It's the kind of pizza that quietly gets the job done while the flashier options are busy trying to be Instagram famous.
Why Clark Kent?
Because it looks pretty ordinary at first, but spend a little time with it and you realise it's actually quite dependable. No cape, no dramatic entrance, just quietly saving dinner from the freezer aisle.
Tasty cheese topping
Easy to cook
Great for a quick meal
Easy to find in-store and online

Overall: A reliable pizza that's better than first impressions suggest. It won't have you texting your mates about it, but it'll happily save the day when cooking is the last thing on your mind.

Comments:
?? The Henry Cavill of Biscuits
These biscuits are dangerously good. Honestly, they probably shouldn't be sold because once the packet is open, self-control immediately leaves the building.
The rich Belgian dark chocolate and warming ginger are a perfect match. Every bite feels a bit luxurious, and before you know it, you're staring at an empty packet wondering what just happened.
Why Henry Cavill?
Because they're classy, handsome, and ridiculously hard to resist. You buy them intending to have one or two, then somehow the whole pack vanishes faster than Superman changing clothes in a phone box.
Rich dark chocolate flavour
Perfect balance of sweet and ginger spice
Easy to find in-store and online
Packet is nowhere near big enough
Overall: One of the best biscuits I've tried. Premium, indulgent, and alarmingly easy to demolish in a single sitting. The only real problem is having the willpower to stop eating them.

???? The Jar Jar Binks of Soups
I had high hopes for this soup. Pea and ham was a childhood favourite, so I was expecting a comforting bowl of smoky goodness. Sadly, this one missed the target.
It was a bit watery, lacked flavour, and never really delivered the rich, hearty taste a pea and ham soup should have. It wasn't awful... just disappointing.
Why Jar Jar Binks?
Because you remember the idea being much better than the reality. It turns up with potential, but leaves you wondering what went wrong.
? Easy to heat up
? Easy to find in-store and online
? Lacking flavour
? Too watery for my taste
Overall: A soup that needed more ham, more smokiness, and a lot more personality. It filled a bowl, but not my expectations.
Character Rating: ???? Jar Jar Binks ? not the worst thing in the galaxy, but definitely not the hero you were hoping for. ???

???? The Deadpool of Salmon
At first glance, this looks like your standard salmon fillet. Then the honey and chilli show up and suddenly things get a lot more interesting.
The salmon was tasty on its own, but the sweet honey and gentle chilli kick gave it a bit of extra personality without taking over. It's not trying to be fancy, it just knows how to make an entrance.
Why Deadpool?

Tasty salmon with a sweet and spicy twist
Easy to find in-store and online
